facts.claim: Elounda Beach Hotel & Villas presents itself and its sister resort Elounda Bay Palace as a choice for weddings, christenings, vows exchange, gala dinners and private celebrations, with waterfront villas and suites that have their own private decks and pools.

Elounda Beach lists a private chapel for weddings and christenings. Its indicative wedding package lists a dedicated consultant, legal and licence paperwork, a civil or religious ceremony outside the hotel's church or at another place of the couple's choice (civil weddings), and an escorted transfer to the authorities to register the wedding.

Elounda Beach publishes banquet capacities (indoor / outdoor): Artemis 180 / 430, Dionysos 100 / 300, Blue Lagoon 70 / 120, Argonaut outdoor 180. At the adjacent Elounda Bay Palace: Aretoussa 300 / 500, Thalassa 100 / 200-400, Ariadne 80 / 150. Largest outdoor cocktail figure listed is Artemis at 650.
facts.conflicts: Re-check of greece-wedding-venues fact_102: figures unchanged on 2026-11-10; page now also lists Blue Lagoon, Thalassa, Ariadne and lounges.

facts.claim: Elounda Beach lists optional wedding services including traditional Cretan lyre music during the ceremony, a firework show, bridal hair and make-up and treatments at the Elounda Beach Spa, and limo transfer for guests.

St. Nicolas Bay Resort Hotel & Villas (Thessi Nissi, Agios Nikolaos, Crete; five-star) has a weddings page: couples celebrate their wedding on the deck of the resort's beachside chapel, with the Cretan Sea behind, on Mirabello Bay.

St. Nicolas Bay says celebrations are tailor-made, from a romantic wedding to a festive family celebration, held in one of the resort's restaurants and bars, with a guest service team for couples; a photographer, fireworks display, music, florist and table decoration can be arranged on request.

St. Nicolas Bay's wedding amenities include a guaranteed upgrade to the Honeymoon Private Pool Suite for the wedding night (subject to its terms), and its accommodation includes seafront suites and villas with private pools. The weddings page publishes no capacity or exclusive-use option.

Minos Beach Art Hotel has a Celebrations and Events page headed 'Your luxury wedding destination in Greece': its team plans weddings, vow renewals and other celebrations at the hotel's waterfront setting, with enquiries through its contact page.
facts.conflicts: Marriott's listing for Minos Beach Art Hotel (a Design Hotels member) answers 'does not provide wedding services' in its events FAQ (seen in a search snippet, not read). The hotel's own site states it hosts weddings; the Advisor should confirm in writing.

facts.claim: Minos Beach Art Hotel describes itself as Crete's original waterfront hideaway, a five-star resort of bungalows and villas with private pools on the water's edge, with two private sandy beaches and about 2 km of coastline, in operation for over 60 years.

Minos Beach Art Hotel's standout is art: a Sculpture Garden and grounds holding over 55 works from the G. & A. Mamidakis Foundation collection. In summer it runs live Cretan nights at its Adeste Kafenio.
Minos Beach Art Hotel states it is about a 50-minute drive from Heraklion Airport (HER), 60 minutes from Heraklion Port and 180 minutes from Chania Airport (CHQ), and can help arrange car transfers.

Elounda Peninsula (All Suite Hotel) has a weddings page: its team offers wedding planning, flower coordination with preferred designers, custom menus from family brunch to a grand reception banquet, table styling and bespoke cakes from the in-house pastry chef, working with the couple or their bridal consultant.

Elounda Peninsula says it can arrange party and photo locations around its hotels, including secluded beaches and historic sites, with advance notice. Its weddings page lists venues across three sister hotels: Elounda Peninsula, Porto Elounda and Elounda Mare Hotel, with one events team for enquiries.

Daios Cove Luxury Resort & Villas (Vathi, Agios Nikolaos) has no weddings page on its own site: its menu lists honeymoon and conferences pages only. The conferences page lists two ballrooms, six meeting rooms and an outdoor events area overlooking the sea, and the honeymoon page mentions an on-site honeymoon planner. It does NOT meet the inclusion rule (run report only).

Elounda Peninsula's wedding packages document (Elounda SA Hotels & Resorts, linked from its weddings page) has separate civil, Greek Orthodox and symbolic (vow renewal) packages. It states symbolic weddings and vow renewals are not legally recognised in Greece.

Elounda Peninsula's civil package covers date and venue reservation, licence paperwork with the local municipality office, two witnesses if needed, ceremony set-up, and a round-trip transfer to the Registry Office. It states the marriage must be registered at the Registry Office in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days, and wedding documents must be emailed at least 4 weeks and couriered at least 3 weeks before the date.
Elounda Peninsula's packages are valid only when the couple stays a minimum of three nights in one of the group's hotels (published package condition, not a guest-wide rule).

Cayo Exclusive Resort & Spa (reserve): its official site (cayoresort.com now redirects to the Mar-Bella Collection page marbella.gr/hotels/cayo) has no weddings page in its menu, and its FAQ does not mention weddings. It sits on the hillside above Plaka near Elounda, about 65 km (about an hour) from Heraklion International Airport, with sea views to Spinalonga. It does NOT meet the inclusion rule (run report only).

St. Nicolas Bay describes a secluded beachfront location about one mile from the town centre of Aghios Nikolaos, and says guests can plan celebrations, private parties and dinners, banquets and romantic weddings at its beachside chapel.

Elounda Peninsula presents itself as a gateway to eastern Crete from the Elounda shore, near Plaka and boat trips to Spinalonga, with sailing and motor yachts available to guests and a Six Senses Spa on site.

Nana Princess (Chersonissos, Crete, on the Aegean coast) has an official weddings page offering civil weddings on its private sandy beach, Greek Orthodox weddings in the private Chapel of St. George in the hotel grounds, symbolic weddings officiated by its event coordinator, and vow renewals; it describes the resort as suited to small to medium sized events. Re-check of Greece pack fact_609.

Nana Princess offers exclusive use of the chosen room or venue for symbolic weddings and vow renewals. Reception options are the terrace of the Eternal Blue restaurant overlooking the bay of Stalis, a poolside reception at the Meat-In-Point restaurant seating up to 120 guests, and the Conference Hall for larger receptions needing a fully covered space. Re-check of Greece pack fact_610.

Nana Princess notes high-summer temperatures in Greece can reach 35 degrees C and recommends evening ceremony times: 16:00 to 18:00 in April, May and October; 18:00 to 20:00 in June to September; 18:30 to 20:00 in July and August. Re-check of Greece pack fact_611.

Nana Princess publishes three named wedding packages (Deluxe Dream, Ultimate Passion, Essential Elegance) and offers bespoke packages; a dedicated event coordinator guides couples through local registry office requirements and other formalities. Re-check of Greece pack fact_612.

Amirandes, Grecotel (north coast of Crete near Heraklion) says on its weddings, meetings and events page that couples can exchange vows at its VIP Beach or in its chapel, choose from diverse dining venues, and plan with dedicated wedding specialists; the page links a wedding request form.

Amirandes lists celebrations of up to 300 guests across its venues, with six meeting rooms and indoor and outdoor spaces; its resort page gives a seaside vow on the VIP Beach for up to 80 guests and a private gathering on the Events Patio for 20 to 160 guests.

Amirandes has 204 accommodations in total (147 rooms, 19 bungalows, 6 duplex suites, 14 suites and 18 private villas, some beachfront with infinity pools), and sits 18 km from Heraklion International Airport (the events page says about 15 minutes) and a short drive from the Palace of Knossos.

Amirandes' architecture draws on Minoan palace design, with lagoons, arches and large handmade pitharia jars, a 960 square metre seawater Olympic-size pool, 58 private pools, and the Minotaur restaurant set among original Pablo Picasso ceramics.

Out of the Blue Resort & Spa (Agia Pelagia, Heraklion, Crete) has an official weddings page: it describes the resort as privately set on a green peninsula, with a dedicated events team and downloadable wedding packages and private venues documents.

Out of the Blue lists Aghios Athanasios Chapel, a small privately owned traditional chapel in the heart of the resort used for prayers, weddings and baptisms, with a garden and sea views where events can take place; outdoor venues Emelia's Secret Garden (Souda Garden) among palm trees and Plateau Safran, a lawn on the edge of the peninsula that can host wedding ceremonies; and restaurants with indoor and outdoor areas for ceremonies and receptions. No guest capacity is stated on the weddings page.

Abaton Island Resort & Spa (Hersonissos, Crete) has an official weddings page: its Wedding & Honeymoon team offers set wedding packages or a custom wedding at the couple's preferred Abaton wedding venue, with a 2025-2026 wedding brochure, and lists ceremony, music, flowers, decor, beauty, cocktail bar, gala dinner, photography and video as options to customise.

Caramel, Grecotel Boutique Resort (Adelianos Kampos, Rethymno, on Crete's north coast) has an official weddings and vow renewals page. It says informal weddings and exchange-of-vows packages are the most popular ceremony at the hotel and that couples do not need to handle paperwork or legal requirements for these, which indicates symbolic (non-legal) ceremonies; no legal ceremony option or capacity is stated on the page.

Abaton's 2025-2026 wedding brochure (linked from its official weddings page) lists nine wedding venues: Elemes, Bony Fish, F-Zin, WOW, Ladies & Gentlemen, Buddha Bar, the Open Air Theatre, the Ballroom and the Beach. Published capacities: Elemes 80, Bony Fish 70, F-Zin 100 indoors or 200 outdoors, WOW 80, Ladies & Gentlemen 200 (ceremony and cocktail only), Buddha Bar 200, Open Air Theatre 200, Ballroom 150; the Beach capacity is not stated.

Abaton's wedding brochure terms say packages need a wedding reception booking of at least 20 guests (maximum capacity 300 guests) and a minimum accommodation booking of 10 rooms for at least 2 nights (depending on guest numbers); the resort offers 152 rooms and villas, 71 with private pools, along the coastline.

Out of the Blue Resort & Spa is spread across its own private peninsula next to the traditional fishing village of Agia Pelagia, with Aegean views, and has three accommodation collections (a modern-art inspired boutique hotel, bungalows, an all-suite hotel, maisonettes and villas with private pools). Room count is not stated on the pages checked.

Caramel sits on Crete's north coast minutes from the historic town of Rethymno, among gardens above a golden-sand beach where caretta caretta sea turtles nest; it describes a retro glamour style with individually designed rooms, a 700 square metre seawater pool, and suites, bungalows, maisonettes and villas, some with private pools. Room count is not stated on the pages checked.

Kapsaliana Village Hotel (Kapsaliana, Rethymno, Crete) has an official Meetings & Events page that presents the restored village for corporate events, small conferences and wellness retreats, accommodating up to 50 people, with 70 seated or 120 for finger food; the page does not mention weddings, so the venue does not meet the inclusion rule on its own site as checked.

Lyrarakis Wines (family winery at Alagni, Heraklion, set among the Psarades vineyard below the Lassithi mountains, producing since 1966) offers wine tastings, vineyard picnics and olive oil tastings on its official visit page; the official site does not present weddings, and the venue site it links (lyrarakis-venue.com) resolved to a parked domain when checked, so the winery does not meet the inclusion rule as checked.

Sea View by En Kipo describes itself as a wedding venue in Chania, Crete: a hilltop garden with panoramic sea and sunset views, offering absolute privacy for weddings, vow renewals and marriage proposals. Its garden is planted with seasonal blooms and Mediterranean greenery cared for by its own florists.

Sea View by En Kipo publishes a maximum of 120 guests for ceremonies and 120 for wedding receptions (dining area up to 120), on 4,200 sq m of free space, with 700 sq m of private parking, a 4.5 m x 4.5 m dance floor, a private air-conditioned dressing room, accessible WC and an emergency power generator.

Sea View by En Kipo says the venue is the couple's exclusively from 10:00am to 12:00am, with the possibility to extend to 2:00am; couples rent the equipment, furniture and decor they want and handpick their own caterer and vendors. Decoration is available on request and the venue works with wedding planners.
facts.conflicts: The venue page lists end time 'up to 24.00' with extension 'on request with extra charge'; the services page says extension possible to 2:00am. Both agree midnight is the standard end time.

facts.claim: Sea View by En Kipo has no guest rooms on site; it offers hospitality support through its team Celmare by EnKipo, arranging accommodation for couples and guests through partner hotels, villas and boutique accommodation in Chania and across Crete. It notes ample private parking, easy highway access and proximity to hotels, restaurants and bars, and lists Chania Airport, Heraklion Airport and Souda Port under 'How to get here'.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's overall advice level for Greece is 'Exercise normal safety precautions' (page updated 30 September 2026, still current at 11 November 2026, re-read live 2026-11-10).

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says wildfires occur in Greece during the extended summer period from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations on the mainland and the islands, prompting evacuations; heatwaves are frequent over the summer months; and Greece is in an active seismic zone, with earthquakes having occurred near Crete and Santorini.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says Australians entering the Schengen area for a short stay (90 days or less in any 180-day period) have fingerprints and a photo taken under the European Entry/Exit System (EES), which is free and needs no action before arrival, and that there may be delays at border crossings, so allow plenty of time for transfers. It also says that during peak season severe traffic congestion occurs on the islands, to use only licensed taxis, and to arrange a coach or taxi pick-up in advance. The Greece page has no marriage-specific section.

As at November 2026, the Australian Embassy in Athens lists among its notarial services witnessing application forms for, and issuing, Certificates of No Impediment (CNI) and witnessing notices of intended marriage, plus legalisation by authentication or apostille. An appointment is needed for all notarial services (CNI and apostille documents can be submitted by post), appointments run Monday to Friday 9:00am to 12:30pm, and CNIs are available for collection within two working days. The Embassy does not provide legal advice, honorary consuls cannot provide notarial services, and fees apply (published on its fees page). The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Getting married overseas' page (last updated 18/08/2026, re-read live 2026-11-10) says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry; the most common documents are a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages; DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need one, whether you can get it in Australia and whether it needs an authentication or apostille. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says an overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia but in most cases is legally recognised if it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law; a foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of marriage but may not be accepted as proof of a name change (check with your local registry); talk to a lawyer to confirm validity. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

Visit Greece (official tourism site) describes Crete as Greece's largest island with over 1,000 km of coastline, and groups it as western Crete (Chania with its Venetian harbour and old town, and Rethymno with its medieval town and Fortezza), central Crete (Heraklion, the largest urban centre and gateway to Knossos, with resorts on the northern coast and Matala in the south) and eastern Crete (Lasithi: Agios Nikolaos and Mirabello Bay, and Elounda, described as the luxury resort with views of the lagoon and Spinalonga).

Chania Airport 'Ioannis Daskalogiannis' (CHQ) is operated by Fraport Greece; its official website lists getting to and from the airport by public bus (direct bus service) and by taxi, plus 24-hour on-site parking.

Visit Greece says Greece has a Mediterranean climate with plenty of sunshine, mild temperatures and limited rainfall; in summer the dry hot days are cooled by seasonal winds called the meltemi, and winters are mild in lowland areas.

Porto Elounda Golf & Spa Resort has its own weddings page ('A Celebration Beyond Imagination') offering venues for ceremonies and parties around its hotels, wedding planning, flower arrangements, custom menus, table decor and bespoke wedding cakes from its in-house Pastry Chef.

Elounda Mare Hotel (a Relais & Chateaux member, per its own site) has its own weddings page with the same Elounda Collection wedding services: venues including secluded beaches and historic sites around the hotels with advance notice, planning, floristry, custom menus and bespoke cakes.

The Porto Elounda and Elounda Mare weddings pages are shared Elounda Collection pages: both link venue and package details for Elounda Peninsula, Porto Elounda and Elounda Mare Hotel and give one events contact (events@elounda-sa.com, +30 28410 68011). Venue capacities are not stated on either page.
facts.conflicts: Porto Elounda and Elounda Mare have no wedding page of their own beyond the shared Elounda Collection page, which also covers Elounda Peninsula (batch A fact_13). Present them as sister venues under one events team, not as independent operators.

facts.claim: Elounda Mare Hotel sits on the shore of Elounda overlooking the bay, is a member of Relais & Chateaux, has a Six Senses spa, and offers main hotel sea view rooms and suites, bungalows with private pool, Minoan Royalty villas with private pool and a four-bedroom beachfront villa, the Minoan Palace, with private pool and direct beach access.

Porto Elounda Golf & Spa Resort sits on the shore of Mirabello Bay, has a golf offering and Six Senses spa, added 74 new suites in 2025 with works on the main veranda, lobby and reception planned for 2026, and says it has the largest seafront pool on Crete. Its Elies restaurant sits beneath an ancient olive grove by the beach.

Elounda Mare, Porto Elounda and Elounda Peninsula are all part of Elounda Collection Hotels & Resorts and share Blue Flag sandy private beaches and restaurants across the three properties (for example Old Mill and Yacht Club at Elounda Mare, Elies and Cosmos at Porto Elounda).

Minos Palace Resort's own Celebrations & Events page ('Luxury Weddings and Your Honeymoon Destination') says its team plans weddings, vow renewals and other celebrations at its seaside, adults-only resort.

Minos Palace Resort describes itself as adults-only on a near-private peninsula with 360-degree views, a private sandy cove beach, an infinity pool with 180-degree sea views, gardens, and a Waterfall Suite with private pool.

Minos Palace Resort is in Lasithi, eastern Crete, and states a 50-minute drive from Heraklion Airport (HER), 60 minutes from Heraklion Port and 180 minutes from Chania Airport (CHQ). It describes eastern Crete weather as pleasant from April to November, with early autumn around 20 to 27 C.

Istron Bay Hotel (Agios Nikolaos) has a page titled 'Wedding' on its own site, but its body text is template copy describing Skiathos and 'Hotel Punta', with no statement about weddings at Istron Bay. It does not meet the inclusion rule on this read.
facts.conflicts: Page title says Wedding but copy is a template about another hotel on Skiathos. Directories claim Istron Bay hosts weddings; those are not usable as sources.

facts.claim: Euphoria Resort has a weddings page offering a special ceremony for an informal wedding or renewal of vows, overlooking the Mediterranean Sea. Each package lists a choice of hotel venues including sun-kissed beaches and poolside settings, with two witnesses and the hotel's official representative, and a certificate of informal marriage from the hotel.

Euphoria Resort's wedding packages are sized for small groups: post-ceremony sparkling wine and cake are listed for up to 10, 20 or 30 guests depending on the package. Other services on request include buffet, seated and cocktail receptions, beverage packages, open bar, custom cakes and entertainment, plus menu tastings, bachelor and bachelorette parties and bridal treatments at the Harmonia Spa.

Avra Imperial Hotel (five-star per its own site description 'Luxury Hotel In Kolymbari Crete') sits next to Kolymvari beach with views of the Rodopou peninsula, and has the private chapel of Saint Paul within the hotel area for wedding ceremonies, plus banqueting rooms and a specialised wedding and group events team.

Avra Imperial lists two reception venues: the central Maistro events hall for up to 680 people, and, for a small reception, a private space by its infinity-style glass pool of 1,500 square metres for alfresco dining. Menus are tailored with the Executive Chef and F&B Manager.
Avra Imperial's weddings page says guests can stay in the hotel's rooms and use treatments at the KORRES Spa, in Kolymvari, Chania.

Minoa Palace Resort (Platanias, Chania, Crete; describes itself as a five-star resort) has a weddings page. Its wedding package lists an ideal location for outdoor or indoor ceremony and reception, customised menus, signature drinks and cocktails, and table decoration consulting on request; extras listed are flower decoration, spa treatments, bridal hair, make-up and manicure, and music options including DJ or live band.

Minoa Palace offers newlyweds a stay in one of its suites after the wedding with local wedding sweets, champagne and flowers, plus room service breakfast the next morning, and a specially decorated wedding cake, all stated as complimentary.

Euphoria Resort is a five-star, Ultra All Inclusive family beach resort on the seashore of Kolymvari, about 14 miles west of Chania, with 344 rooms and suites (including a 70-key Signature Collection) on a 65,000 sq m sea-front property, a 3,500 sq m pool area and a 1,500 sq m spa. A member of EM Resorts (the same group as Minoa Palace).
facts.conflicts: Same homepage gives the drive from Chania International Airport (CHQ) as 30 minutes (meta description) and 40 minutes (body text). [[VERIFY: Euphoria Resort transfer time from Chania Airport, 30 or 40 minutes]]

insider_details.detail: Elounda and Agios Nikolaos are a Heraklion Airport destination: Minos Beach Art Hotel puts its drive at about 50 minutes and Cayo near Plaka at about an hour (65 km), while Chania Airport is about three hours from Minos Beach. Book guests into Heraklion, not Chania, for an east Crete wedding.

For a legal civil wedding in the Elounda area, plan for paperwork after the party: Elounda Peninsula's package states the marriage must be registered at the Registry Office in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days, and both Elounda Peninsula and Elounda Beach build an escorted trip to the authorities into their packages. Keep a weekday free in the itinerary.

Documents for a Greek civil ceremony take weeks, not days: Elounda Peninsula asks for copies by email at least 4 weeks out and originals by courier at least 3 weeks out, with each document carrying its own apostille and a Greek translation. Australians should start the Certificate of No Impediment and apostilles well before that.

Elounda Beach is the east Crete option for a big guest list: its published banquet figures run to 430 outdoors at Artemis, and the adjacent Elounda Bay Palace's Aretoussa lists 500 outdoors. St. Nicolas Bay and Minos Beach publish no capacities, so ask for a written figure before shortlisting them for 100-plus guests.

Package minimum stays apply to the couple, not necessarily the guests: Elounda Peninsula's packages need the couple to stay at least three nights in one of its hotels. Ask each venue separately about minimum nights for a room block or buyout.

A symbolic ceremony at a resort is not a legal marriage in Greece (Elounda Peninsula says so in its own package notes). Couples who want the ceremony at the chapel or on the beach without Greek paperwork can marry legally in Australia first.

Nana Princess publishes its own ceremony timing guide: late afternoon (16:00 to 18:00) in April, May and October, and no earlier than 18:00 from June to September, so build the transfer and photography schedule backwards from an evening ceremony.

Amirandes is the most airport-friendly option in this group at 18 km from Heraklion International Airport, which suits guests arriving on staggered flights; its 204 rooms and 18 private villas also make it possible to keep most of a guest list on one site.
Amirandes caps a beach ceremony at 80 guests, while the Events Patio takes 20 to 160, so couples with a larger list should plan the vows and the reception in different spaces.
Abaton is one of the few Crete resorts to publish its wedding terms: packages assume at least 20 reception guests and a block of at least 10 rooms for 2 nights, so confirm your room block early.
Out of the Blue sits on its own peninsula with a private chapel and two lawn venues at the water's edge, so the ceremony, photos and reception can all happen without guests leaving the resort.
Caramel frames its weddings as informal vow ceremonies with no paperwork, which suits couples who complete the legal marriage in Australia and want a relaxed beach celebration in Rethymno.

Sea View by En Kipo hands the couple the venue from morning to midnight and lets them bring their own caterer, bar and hire furniture, so the budget and supplier list are built from scratch: book an experienced planner early and lock caterer, lighting and transport together.

Sea View by En Kipo has no rooms on site, so guests stay in Chania hotels and villas and every guest needs a planned coach to and from the hilltop; its own accommodation team can help assemble a room block, and the venue lists both Chania and Heraklion airports under how to get there.
Treat 120 as a hard ceiling at Sea View by En Kipo: the venue publishes the same maximum for ceremony and reception, so a guest list near that number leaves no room for late additions.

For summer dates, build a heat and wildfire plan into the run sheet: Smartraveller flags June to September wildfires near tourist areas on the islands and frequent summer heatwaves, so allow shade, water and a flexible transfer plan, and keep a guest contact list for any disruption.

Allow buffer time on arrival day: Smartraveller notes EES biometric registration for Australians entering the Schengen area and possible border delays, plus peak-season traffic on the islands, so do not schedule welcome events tight against guests' landing times.

Start the paperwork in Athens, not Crete: the Australian Embassy in Athens issues Certificates of No Impediment by appointment (or by post) with collection within two working days, so build that step into the legal timeline well before the wedding week.

Porto Elounda, Elounda Mare and Elounda Peninsula share one weddings page and one events contact, and their guests share beaches and restaurants across the three. A couple can hold the ceremony at one and house family at another, but should ask the single events team which venue suits each part of the day.
Minos Palace Resort is adults-only. For families bringing children, confirm in writing whether under-age wedding guests can attend or stay before shortlisting it.
Minos Palace publishes 50 minutes from Heraklion Airport and three hours from Chania Airport, the same pattern batch A found for Minos Beach. East Crete guests should fly into Heraklion.

Porto Elounda has been mid-renovation (74 new suites in 2025, veranda, lobby and reception works planned for 2026). Ask for current photos of the spaces you will use and a written completion date before signing.

Kolymvari is the far west of the Chania coast: Euphoria Resort puts itself about 14 miles west of Chania town and 30 to 40 minutes from Chania Airport, and Avra Imperial sits on the same bay. Fly guests into Chania, not Heraklion, and plan one coach run for the whole group rather than staggered taxis.

Avra Imperial suits both ends of the guest list: a private chapel on site for the ceremony, then either the Maistro hall (up to 680) for a large Greek-style reception or the 1,500 sq m pool terrace for a small alfresco dinner. Ask early which one your number fits, since the page does not give the terrace capacity.

Euphoria Resort's own packages stop at 30 guests and describe the ceremony as an informal wedding or vow renewal, so treat it as a symbolic-ceremony option, with the legal paperwork done separately, unless the Wedded Advisor confirms otherwise.
